item.title: Future Scholars in Business and Society: Current Work and Emerging Directions
item.content:encoded:
Barrie Litzky, Drexel University

This special issue of Business and Society Review seeks doctoral research exploring the relationship between business and society. The journal welcomes emerging scholarship that addresses ethical challenges, corporate responsibility, stakeholder relations, sustainability, and social innovation, as well as newer concerns like technology and artificial intelligence. The issue aims to provide doctoral students with a venue to present novel questions, perspectives, and methodological approaches that advance the field.

Submissions may be at various stages of development, from defended dissertation proposals to more advanced work with preliminary findings. Both empirical and conceptual studies are welcome. Manuscripts must be authored exclusively by doctoral students or teams of doctoral students, with faculty members limited to informal advisory roles. All submissions will undergo standard double-blind peer review and follow the journal's formatting guidelines.

Appel publié par Business and Society Review. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Ethical decision-making and moral responsibility
  • Stakeholder theory and engagement
  • Inequality, precarity, and justice
  • Sustainability and social innovation
  • Technology, AI, and data ethics
  • Institutional and global perspectives on business-society issues
  • Corporate governance and responsibility
  • Business-government relations and policy
  • Conceptual and theoretical advancements
  • Pedagogical research in ethics and CSR

  • Invalid DateTime: Expected Publication
  • December 15, 2026: Special Issue Manuscript Submissions Open
  • March 30, 2027: Special Issue Manuscript Submission Deadline

item.title: New-age Technologies Driven Strategic Marketing for a Better World
item.content:encoded:
Chiara Civera, University of Turin

Demetris Vrontis, University of Nicosia

Sanjit K. Roy, Edith Cowan University

Valentina Chiaudano, University of Turin

The special issue examines how emerging technologies like artificial intelligence, machine learning, and blockchain can reshape marketing strategies toward a multi-stakeholder approach in global contexts. While firms increasingly deploy advanced technologies to enhance customer engagement and personalization, there is limited understanding of how these technologies can support marketing that simultaneously addresses the interests of employees, suppliers, regulators, communities, and society. The issue seeks to bridge this gap by exploring how NATs enable stakeholder engagement, value creation, and governance across global marketing ecosystems.

Appel publié par Journal of Strategic Marketing. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Artificial Intelligence and Value Co-Creation in Global Marketing Ecosystems: how AI and advanced technologies reshape marketing strategies, processes, and interactions among multiple stakeholders in global markets; how NATs enable new forms of value co-creation among firms, customers, suppliers, regulators, and communities; how technology-enabled marketing infrastructures enhance transparency and coordination across global value chains
  • Governance, Ethics, and Responsible AI in Marketing: ethical, governance, and organizational implications of NAT-driven marketing systems; algorithmic bias, transparency, accountability, and fairness in data-driven marketing practices; governance mechanisms and organizational capabilities for implementing responsible and transparent NAT-enabled marketing strategies; managing stakeholder tensions and trade-offs arising from NAT-supported marketing decisions
  • Cross-Country Dynamics of New-age Technologies in Marketing: how institutional environments, cultural contexts, and regulatory frameworks influence the adoption and governance of artificial intelligence in global marketing; cross-country differences in implementation of NAT-enabled marketing strategies; how new-age technologies influence global marketing strategy and ecosystem coordination; how NATs support sustainable, inclusive, and responsible marketing practices in global markets

Timeline

  • April 30, 2027: Manuscript submission deadline

item.title: Sustainability by Projects: Rethinking Stakeholder Engagement, Legacy, and Impact
item.content:encoded:
Kirsi Aaltonen, University of Oulu

Siavash Alimadadi, King's College London

Marina Bos-de Vos, Delft University of Technology

Ermal Hetemi, KTH Royal Institute of Technology

Projects increasingly serve as platforms for translating sustainability goals into concrete actions, yet the relationship between stakeholder engagement and sustainability outcomes is complex and multifaceted. This special issue examines how projects and programs generate, mediate, and shape sustainability outcomes and legacies through stakeholder engagement across their entire lifecycle, extending beyond traditional project success metrics to encompass long-term societal and environmental impacts.

The special issue identifies five central tensions: the paradox of inclusion and exclusion in stakeholder participation; the mismatch between global sustainability ambitions and local contextual realities; conflicts between project temporal constraints and extended sustainability time horizons; tensions between managerial control approaches and emergent sustainability dynamics; and the reconfiguring influence of artificial intelligence on stakeholder engagement processes. These tensions reflect competing demands and values that cannot be fully resolved simultaneously but require careful conceptual and empirical examination.

Appel publié par Project Management Journal. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Inclusion, exclusion, and stakeholder voice in projects and how these dynamics shape legitimacy and sustainability outcomes
  • Global ambitions and local realities: how global sustainability goals are interpreted, translated, and contested in local project contexts
  • Project temporality and sustainability time horizons: tensions between short-term delivery pressures and long-term sustainability objectives
  • Managerial control and emergent sustainability dynamics: control-oriented approaches versus emergent and value-laden aspects of sustainability
  • Artificial intelligence and the reconfiguration of tensions: how AI shapes stakeholder engagement, participation, bias, accountability, and legitimacy in sustainability-oriented projects
  • Sustainable project legacy: long-term value and lasting impacts that projects leave for communities and the environment
  • Stakeholder engagement mechanisms through which sustainability outcomes are negotiated, contested, and realized
  • Power asymmetries and their role in shaping sustainability outcomes and project trajectories
  • Temporal work and how actors mobilize visions of futures to coordinate action across divergent timeframes
  • Portfolio governance, intermediary organizational structures, and their mediation between strategic sustainability ambitions and project delivery practices

Timeline

item.title: Creating, Measuring, and Managing Impact in Complex Service Systems
item.content:encoded:
Ting Yu, University of New South Wales

Ko de Ruyter, King's College London

Che-Hun Liao, Kaohsiung City government

This special issue addresses how research generates tangible impact within complex, interdependent service systems such as healthcare, education, and public administration. Despite growing pressure to prove research impact, evidence of meaningful change in complex service contexts remains limited and difficult to measure due to multiple actors, competing interests, and extended timeframes.

The issue seeks robust empirical evidence showing how research translates into observable improvements in user behavior, service processes, organizational practices, or policy. Contributions using diverse methodologies—qualitative, quantitative, mixed-method, experimental, or participatory—are encouraged. Particularly valued are works addressing how impact is assessed across stakeholders, what roles co-creation plays, and ethical dimensions including power asymmetries, unintended consequences, and underrepresented voices.

Appel publié par European Journal of Marketing. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Impact assessment frameworks and metrics in service systems
  • Research impact beyond financial metrics
  • Interdependencies and governance in complex services
  • Impact trajectories and value distribution
  • Change mechanisms and stakeholder engagement
  • Longitudinal and field-based evidence collection
  • Co-creation and stakeholder collaboration
  • Intervention and design-based research outcomes
  • Policy and practice change
  • Scaling and sustainability of research impact
  • Intended and unintended consequences of research
  • Ethical considerations in impact measurement
  • Power dynamics and outcome valuation
  • Differential stakeholder impacts
  • Underrepresented stakeholder voices
  • Managing unequal stakeholder impacts
  • Professional and societal interest alignment

Timeline

  • January 2, 2027: Opening date for manuscripts submissions
  • March 31, 2027: Closing date for manuscripts submission
